To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the climate effects of aerosols are complex, but that the effects of aerosol radiative forcing are the most important.

(a) aerosol optical depth and single-scatter albedo are strongly correlated, (b) aerosol single-scatter albedos are highly variable, and (c) single-scattering properties are highly correlated with the aerosol size distribution.

(1) aerosol particles exert a substantial influence upon the Earth's climate, (2) this influence is complex and depends upon the size, composition, and mixing state of the aerosols, (3) the influence of aerosols upon climate is poorly known, and (4) the influence of anthropogenic aerosols upon climate may be comparable to that of greenhouse gases.
In summary, our research is concerned with
improving our understanding of the role of tropospheric particles in the Earth's radiation budget.
understanding the physical and chemical properties of atmospheric aerosol particles, their interactions with radiation, and their effects on cloud formation and precipitation.
improving the representation of tropospheric climate effects of aerosols in climate models.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

aerosol properties and effects are important to climate, that the representation of them in global climate models needs to be improved, and that a systematic program of field and laboratory studies is needed to provide the foundation for such improvement.
the U.S. DOE program has been very successful in developing a strategy for improving the treatment of aerosol properties and effects in global climate models and has begun to implement that strategy.
the aerosols are the most important and most uncertain factor in climate forcing.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the aerosol module is now ready to be implemented in the global climate models.
aerosol properties and their effects on climate have been studied in great detail, but that the processes responsible for aerosol properties and aerosol-climate interactions are not well understood.
aerosol properties and aerosol processes are being studied at the fundamental level, with a focus on the most critical processes for climate change.
The main takeaway from our work is that
aerosol properties and their effects can be represented in a global climate model with a relatively modest increase in computational cost.
the current state-of-the-art global climate models (GCMs) do not adequately represent aerosols and their effects on the climate system.
the aerosol optical depth (AOD) is a very important quantity in the context of climate change, because it is a key parameter that determines the magnitude of the aerosol radiative forcing (ARF).
